goal: Future-proof FORGE by separating canonical contracts, dynamic runner result roles, import state, and consultant UI copy before adding more feature work.
principles: Keep the Tampermonkey install simple, but stop treating the userscript source as the only system boundary.
Use one canonical role vocabulary across drawer, W144 adapter, runner result capture, import guard, display, and harnesses.
Let operating mode define required, optional, expected, partial, and invalid records.
Treat website evidence as the naming authority, toggles as operating-model authority, and notes as story/ROI/coaching authority.
Keep drawer no-write boundaries intact while making runner-created records easier to inspect and trust.

canonicalContractFilesToIntroduce.purpose: Define retail_availability, apparel_style_matrix, dealer_hardgoods_replenishment, distribution_replenishment, discrete_manufacturing, wip_manufacturing, and food_batch_manufacturing record contracts.

Define canonical runner/import/display roles such as customer, sales_order, finished_food_or_batch_item, ingredient_or_component_item, formula_or_batch_structure, work_order_or_wip_object, routing, and work_center.
Define Build lifecycle states and consultant/admin copy for ready, submitted, waiting, completed_result_found, imported, partial, failed, and recovery.
Centralize numeric internal id and supported NetSuite URL validation.

legacyFiveRecordAssumptionInventory.risk: Adapter can reject or misread valid dynamic-mode requests that do not fit the old five-record shape.

legacyFiveRecordAssumptionInventory.lineHint: normalizeCompletedRunnerResult maps only customer, demoTransaction, heroItem, matrixProofItem, and first componentItem.
legacyFiveRecordAssumptionInventory.risk: Returned formula, lot, routing, work center, work order, or extra manufacturing records can be dropped before FORGE sees them.

legacyFiveRecordAssumptionInventory.lineHint: dccFinalNavigationModel uses scriptPivotObjects derived from a sliced object list.
legacyFiveRecordAssumptionInventory.risk: Build can show a returned record while Run omits it from consultant guidance.

legacyFiveRecordAssumptionInventory.lineHint: Userscript contains contracts, resolver, UI, trace, import guards, branding, and state machine in one large file.
legacyFiveRecordAssumptionInventory.risk: Small wording or UI changes can accidentally affect runner/import behavior.

legacyFiveRecordAssumptionInventory.lineHint: Runner still contains fallback naming and generic-mode branches.
legacyFiveRecordAssumptionInventory.risk: Website/toggle authority can be diluted by generic fallback terms if the completed result is not role-validated.

dynamicRunnerResultShapeTarget.rule: FORGE imports by role array and mode contract, not by fixed legacy slots.

buildLifecycleStateMachine.consultantCopy: Core build records are ready. Some detail was not returned.

buildLifecycleStateMachine.allowedAction: Ask admin to review and retry

recommendedRefactorSequence: Add source modules while preserving generated idb-drawer.user.js output.
Move contracts and copy matrices into src/contracts first.
Teach W144 adapter to validate requiredRecordRoles instead of fixed five requiredRecords.
Teach adapter normalization to preserve a dynamic records array and map legacy fields into roles only as compatibility input.
Teach Run and Build to render all openable returned records by role, without slicing away mode-required records.
Keep reports, trace samples, and older data as archive/evidence rather than runtime authority.
